reviews.comment: He's sort of funny but I HEAVILY relied on outside tutoring for this class, lectures didn't really help. He writes fast and messy. Do the HW since they're extra credit and the questions will also become iClicker questions. Final grade replaces the lowest exam. Honestly Spartan has better methods for this class, way faster than what Akimov does.

I loved Professor Akimov! the final replaces your lowest grade. DO THE HOMEWORK, the homework is optional but in the end, it's extra credit. I got a 41,32, 68, and a 59 on the final and managed to pass with a C. He is very caring and actually cares about your grade and you can always ask for a regrade.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Akimov is one of the better choices for E&M. Its a hard class and theres no way around that, but he does his best to break down complex topics. Recitation is super helpful, I highly recommend going. He does have an accent but its easy to understand. Only complaint is that he can spend too long on derivations that arent very important to us.

Has a strong accent so if you're like me and don't do well with them, avoid this class. Writes on a small whiteboard in the corner of the classroom which is barely visible. The canvas page is totally lacking and incomplete with the slides and review material.

Akimov is pretty good. He does have an accent, but he's knowledgeable, and I felt like I learned the material (or at least how to do the problems). It's Don't Panic, so be ready to use variables, but go to recitation and do old exams before the test and you should do fine. Lecture is pretty interesting, and there are iclicker questions.

Akimov's lectures aren't all that helpful for solving practice exams, but it helps a ton with getting overall concepts. He's a really nice guy in-office hours and helped with anything I was confused about. I will say the recitation was the only reason I ended up getting an A in the course, and I HIGHLY recommend going. (GET THE BOOK)

You cannot go wrong with Dr. Akimov. He is very willing to help you do well in this course. He is big on teaching derivations but when it comes to the test most of the derivations arent necessary. No matter the teacher you need to put effort into class. As long as you go to SI and do a lot of the practice tests then you are solid.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Akimov teaches physics well enough to learn it, but he can go a little fast for some people, so if you don't pick up on everything too quickly, it might be hard to follow. He has a fairly dark sense of humor but does joke relatively often in class. Overall, I enjoyed the class, and I plan to take him for 208.
Like all other profs for 218, your grade is almost entirely based on your tests. His lectures are as fun as physics can be and he is a pretty generous grader.

I didn't get a lot of Akimov's lectures, to be honest. The lectures more-so showed you how you can apply the formulas, I really learned a lot on my own and from my recitation leader. GO TO RECITATION!!! The labs are easy, and Akimov's ready to sit down with you for hours during office hours to make sure you get what you're doing. He's a great guy.

Alexey is a great professor and a funny guy. He typically works out the most difficult problems from each chapter in class on the whiteboard, which makes the exam questions seem relatively easy and straightforward. If you make sure that you fully understand how to do the homework and recitation problems, you will get an easy A.
Dr. Akimov really makes an effort to be accessible outside of class. He is a great prof and I would recommend him for 218.

Akimov is incredibly smart, which is both great and not so great. He probably has the best methodology Ive ever seen for Physics, but because hes so smart, he goes really fast. But if you can keep up, and stay on track, you shouldnt have any more problems than any other Physics student. Its a fairly hard course, highly conceptual.

He made an extremely difficult course a bit less difficult. He tells jokes in lecture to keep our attention and would bring in models to allow us to visualize tough topics. He addressed most of the FlipIt questions asked and was available during office hours to discuss any questions you had on the exam or grade received.

Let me cut to the chase, on the first exam, I got a 46, second, 54, third, 58. On the final, I got a 74 and ended with a B as my entire course grade. What I am saying is, do not give up over this course. It is very challenging, but this professor helps you a lot. In office hours he is willing to spend HOURS with you until you learn the material.
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Akimov is a great professor. He genuinely cares about his students and is there to help you pass the class-especially if he knows you well. Therefore GO TO OFFICE HOURS as much as possible!! Also DO try hard on homework, clickers, and labs to get as many points as possible. Also the profs are NOT in charge of L.O. percentage so don't blame them

iClicker questions in class (but you should get all points if you just show up). Physics 218 is hard no matter who you take, but Prof Akimov is probably the best option. GO TO OFFICE HOURS, he explains what you didnt get on test and why and it is very helpful. He has an accent, but is kinda funny and it doesnt get in the way.

Super nice, caring, and funny. Lectures are not super helpful (I learned mostly through homework), but there are iClicker quizzes. Always had office hours and gives good feedback. Stereotypical Russian accent is also pretty cool. Would definitely suggest taking him!

Physics is a difficult class any way about it, and Akimov is smart enough that he tends to lose students during lecture. If you can formulate specific questions, either in office hours or during lecture, he can answer them and help clarify whatever you don't understand.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I walked into this class as a homeschooler who hadn't ever taken physics, and Prof. Akimov makes this class great (you don't have to have AP Physics to make a B or higher). He genuinely cares and tries to help, so go to his office hours. He's really funny. Additionally, if you're struggling in his classes, try going to A+ tutoring.

I hate physics so much, but Akimov managed to make it almost enjoyable. He's really funny and clearly knows the material very well. His lectures are entertaining. He does have a Russian accent, but it's not a problem at all, however his terrible handwriting can be occasionally.

Professor Akimov is one of the best Physics 218 professors. He makes lectures interesting and enjoyable. He is SUPER helpful in office hours and gives great review sessions before every class. Sit in the front and ask/answer questions. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: He's Russian and his accent is easy to understand so there's no language barrier other than physics-talk. The tests are common exams so the reviews are useless to study with in my opinion. When you fail your first exam, don't get discouraged because there's a giant curve over the entire course. Also, expect a lot of online homework and tears.

Physics is hard. That is a given, but with Akimov as my professor it was my favorite class of the semester. He is hilarious and explains things really well. Our class always got the highest averages on exams. He had Darth Vader and Chuck Norris in one of his lectures. AKA get him if you can. He's bomb diggety. Best prof for physics in my opinion.

All the tests are common, so choosing one professor over another comes down to teaching preference. Dr. Akimov knows the material very well, and encourages questions. His sense of humor gives lectures some life. Do the prelectures, or read before class and you will find his lectures enjoyable.

His sense of humor keeps class entertaining. He also has a good dialogue with the students and encourages participation. He is very good about answering questions in lecture and will use demos to illustrate concepts. The TA for my section was what made the course great. Physics is hard for anyone but with Akimov its do-able.
